correctness.rationale: An exact finite-jump formula and uniformly controlled one-cell power expansion give a pathwise leading error. Joint equidistribution of Poisson arrival-time phases under arbitrary bounded old-process multipliers follows from absolute continuity and Fourier approximation. The two meshes share the phase U and {2U}; their difference equals a fair Bernoulli per jump, giving the exact conditional variance. Reproducibility code checks algebra only; no finite experiment establishes the stable convergence.

value.rationale: Two-level coupling is central to multilevel simulation and is not determined by separate single-level limits. A shared uniform jump phase collapses under dyadic differencing to a discrete Bernoulli mark with exact nonzero conditional variance, a natural sharp diagnostic for coupled simulations. This is a self-contained finite-activity benchmark, not a claim of broad algorithmic advances.
